Apply consistent trimming warnings to JS interop serialization APIs.

## Description

Synchronous JS interop APIs carry `RequiresUnreferencedCode`, while corresponding async APIs omit it. `DynamicallyAccessedMembers` does not cover nested object graphs or arbitrary serialized arguments, so both annotations remain necessary.

Issues.Body:

- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Rethrow the app's startup exception instead of ObjectDisposedException

## Description

When the app under test fails in `IHost.StartAsync`, `app.Run()` disposes the host before the entry point exits. If that happens before `DeferredHost.StartAsync` resolves `IHostApplicationLifetime`, `WebApplicationFactory` throws `ObjectDisposedException` and the real startup exception is lost.

`DeferredHost.StartAsync` now skips the `ApplicationStarted` registration when the host is already disposed and keeps awaiting the start TCS. The entry point is exiting at that point, and `HostFactoryResolver` reports its completion in a `finally`, so `EntryPointCompleted` always completes the TCS with the app's exception or result. The success and cancellation paths are unchanged.

The regression test uses `SimpleWebSiteWithWebApplicationBuilder` with a failing `ValidateOnStart`. Its factory holds `CreateHost` until the app's service provider has been disposed, which makes the ordering deterministic. Without the fix it failed 10/10 runs with the reported `ObjectDisposedException` stack. With the fix it passed 10/10, and `Mvc.FunctionalTests` passes in full (1669 passed, 3 skipped).

Fixes #69684

# Fix SignalR fallback authorization for non-authorization metadata

- [x] You've read the [[Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [[Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [ ] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making.

Prevent non-authorization hub metadata from triggering fallback authorization

## Description

SignalR hub method authorization used the presence of any method authorization metadata to determine whether authorization should run.

This caused metadata that does not define an authorization policy, such as `[AllowAnonymous]` or an unrelated attribute, to enter the authorization path. When `AuthorizationPolicy.CombineAsync` found no applicable `IAuthorizeData`, `AuthorizationPolicy`, or `IAuthorizationRequirementData`, the configured fallback policy was applied instead.

With a fallback policy requiring an authenticated user, this caused anonymous hub method invocations to be rejected unexpectedly.

This change ensures that hub method authorization is only performed when the metadata contains authorization-relevant data.

The regression test `AnonymousConnectionCanInvokeMethodsOnAllowAnonymousHubWithFallbackPolicy` covers:

- Async method without additional attributes
- Async method with `[AllowAnonymous]`
- Async method with an explicit open authorization policy
- Synchronous method without additional attributes
- Synchronous method with `[AllowAnonymous]`
- Method with unrelated metadata

The full SignalR test suite was also run successfully after the change.

Note: The standalone reproduction in the issue reports `AsyncNoAttribute` as unauthorized on .NET 11 RC1. That specific behavior was not reproduced by the lower-level `HubConnectionHandlerTests` test infrastructure, where a method with no authorization metadata bypasses method authorization. The regression test reproduces the `[AllowAnonymous]` and unrelated-metadata failures addressed by this change.

Fixes #69624

> AI assistance was used to help understand the existing test structure and to prepare this pull request description.

Issues.Title: DBSC: full support for multiple DBSC schemes, including testing and validation
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The experimental DBSC implementation (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.DeviceBoundSessions`) was designed and tested around a single DBSC scheme wrapping a single source cookie scheme. `AddDeviceBoundSession` is callable multiple times, but multi-scheme behavior was never specified, implemented end to end, or validated. This issue tracks full support for multiple DBSC schemes, including design, implementation, testing, and validation, as a requirement for any reintroduction of DBSC.

Related to #66478 (DBSC tracking), #68117 (API proposal), #68520 (scheme-convention alignment), #69619 (derived cookies should inherit the source `DataProtectionProvider`), and #67794 (shared `ITicketStore`). The implementation was removed from .NET 11 by #69462, so this tracks a requirement for the reintroduction rather than a servicing change. Code links refer to the last `main` commit before the removal, `b3d5795c6f`.

## Problem: Data Protection isolation is only partially scheme-scoped

DBSC protects data in two places, and they behave differently with several schemes.

| Protected value | Created by | Purpose chain includes the scheme? |
|---|---|---|
| Refresh cookie | Cookie authentication (derived scheme `{source}.Dbsc.Refresh`) | Yes: `CookieAuthenticationMiddleware`, `{derivedScheme}`, `v2` |
| Session cookie | Cookie authentication (derived scheme `{source}.Dbsc.Session`) | Yes |
| Registration challenge | `DeviceBoundSessionChallengeProtector` | **No**: fixed `…Challenge.Registration.v1` |
| Refresh challenge | `DeviceBoundSessionChallengeProtector` | **No**: fixed `…Challenge.Refresh.v1` |

Consequences with two or more DBSC schemes:

* A challenge minted for scheme A unprotects successfully on scheme B. The only binding is the principal claim UID (and the session id for refresh), not the scheme. Registration and refresh challenges are separated from each other by purpose, but not between schemes.
* `DeviceBoundSessionChallengeProtector` is registered once as a singleton (`DeviceBoundSessionExtensions.AddDeviceBoundSessionCore`) and uses the application-default `IDataProtectionProvider`. It cannot use a different provider per DBSC scheme.
* `DeviceBoundSessionHandler` also constructs its own `DeviceBoundSessionChallengeProtector` instance, while `DeviceBoundSessionRegistrationHeader` resolves the DI singleton to mint the registration challenge. The two only agree today because both use the default provider.
* Once #69619 makes derived cookies use the source scheme's provider, challenges would still use the default provider. With a dedicated or persisted source provider, cookies would survive a restart or another instance while challenges would not.

Affected code:

* `DeviceBoundSessionChallengeProtector.cs` (constructor): fixed purposes, no scheme.
* `DeviceBoundSessionHandler.cs` (constructor): creates its own challenge protector from the default provider.
* `DeviceBoundSessionRegistrationHeader.cs`: resolves the singleton challenge protector.
* `DeviceBoundSessionExtensions.cs` (`AddDeviceBoundSessionCore`): `TryAddSingleton<DeviceBoundSessionChallengeProtector>()`.
* `PostConfigureCookieAuthenticationOptions.cs` (core cookies): shows the scheme-keyed purpose that DBSC cookies already get.

Recommended direction: make challenge protection per DBSC scheme and rooted in the source scheme's effective `DataProtectionProvider`, with the DBSC scheme name in the purpose chain.

```csharp
var provider = cookieOptionsMonitor.Get(options.RegistrationSourceScheme).DataProtectionProvider;
provider.CreateProtector(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.DeviceBoundSessions.Challenge.Registration.v1",
    dbscSchemeName);
```

The handler already has `Options.RegistrationSourceScheme` and an `IOptionsMonitor<CookieAuthenticationOptions>`, and the registration header already receives the resolved DBSC scheme, so one per-scheme protector (for example from a factory or cache keyed by scheme) can serve both. Changing the purposes invalidates in-flight challenges, which is acceptable because the package is experimental.

## Other multi-scheme areas to specify and validate

Data Protection is not the only area. The following also need an explicit design and tests:

* **Endpoint path collisions.** `RegistrationPath` and `RefreshPath` default to the same values (`/.well-known/dbsc/registration` and `/refresh`) for every DBSC scheme. `HandleRequestAsync` matches on method and path only, so with default paths the first handler registered answers every request, and registration or refresh runs against the wrong source scheme. Options validation only checks that registration and refresh differ within one scheme. Decide between per-scheme paths, a distinguishing component, or failing fast on a cross-scheme collision.
* **Refresh cookie path scoping.** The derived refresh cookie path is the directory of the scheme's `RefreshPath`. Confirm that cookies of different schemes sharing a directory do not interfere, and that paths remain correct under a path base. Related to #69618 and #67850.
* **Default authenticate scheme handling.** `PostConfigureDeviceBoundSessionAuthenticationOptions` only upgrades the app's default authenticate scheme when it matches a DBSC source scheme. Define behavior for apps using several DBSC source schemes, including per-request forwarding (#69620).
* **Shared state in `DeviceBoundSessionSourceSchemes`.** The scheme maps are keyed by source scheme. Define and test behavior when the same source scheme is registered twice or when derived names collide, and fail with a clear error.
* **Per-scheme source configuration.** Source schemes may differ in cookie settings, `DataProtectionProvider`, `TicketDataFormat`, `SessionStore` (#67794), and events. Derived schemes must follow their own source, not another one.
* **Registration exchange guard.** `DeviceBoundSessionCookieEvents.RegistrationExchangeItemKey` is a single `HttpContext.Items` key. Confirm it cannot suppress sign-out handling for a different scheme within one request.
* **Documentation.** Document the supported multi-scheme topologies and their limits, including Data Protection behavior and path configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A registration challenge issued for DBSC scheme A is rejected by scheme B, even when both schemes share the same `DataProtectionProvider` and the same principal.
* [ ] A refresh challenge issued for scheme A is rejected by scheme B, even with the same principal and session id.
* [ ] Challenges use the effective `DataProtectionProvider` of their own source scheme. A challenge minted under a dedicated provider cannot be validated under the application-default provider, and the reverse also fails.
* [ ] Challenge minting (registration header) and validation (handler) resolve the same per-scheme protector.
* [ ] Source, refresh, and session cookies of all schemes remain pairwise non-interchangeable (extends `DerivedCookieSchemes_RemainDataProtected_AndSchemeKeyed`).
* [ ] Two DBSC schemes with the default paths either work correctly or fail at startup with a clear message. Requests are never handled by the wrong scheme.
* [ ] Registration, refresh, session cookie issuance, and sign-out work independently for two DBSC schemes within one app, each with its own source scheme and settings.
* [ ] Tests use the real `AddCookie` and `AddDeviceBoundSession` registration pipeline, not only direct `PostConfigure` calls, so options ordering is covered. They cover at least two schemes, with both shared and distinct providers.
* [ ] An end-to-end validation with two schemes is documented, using the `DbscDebugServer` sample or equivalent, to confirm the browser flow.
* [ ] Multi-scheme behavior and its limits are documented, and #66478 records this requirement before DBSC is reintroduced.

Issues.Title: Request Delegate Generator: handlers that differ only by a parameter's default value share one interceptor, InvalidCastException at startup
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Related: #66912 and its fix #67591, which made the grouping of endpoints compare the binding source, the lookup name and optionality, but not the default value.

With `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator` (on by default under `PublishAot` and `PublishTrimmed`), these two endpoints share one interceptor:

```csharp
app.MapGet("/page-1", (int page = 1) => $"page {page}");
app.MapGet("/page-2", (int page = 2) => $"page {page}");
```

The interceptor casts the handler to the first lambda's natural type, `Cast(handler, global::System.String (global::System.Int32 arg0= 1) => throw null!)` (line 182 of the generated file, the `MapGet0` frame below), and writes `page_parsed_temp = 1;` as the fallback. The second lambda's natural type is another anonymous delegate type, so `MapGet` throws `InvalidCastException` at startup.

The default value has never been part of the comparison. On `main` (and `release/11.0`), `EndpointParameter.Equals` and `GetHashCode` compare `Source`, `SymbolName`, `LookupName`, `Ordinal`, `IsOptional`, `Type` and `KeyedServiceKey`, not `HasDefaultValue` and `DefaultValue` ([EndpointParameter.cs#L595-L616 at aaec58f](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/aaec58f9ccee7962c6071b36f5b17eb07af0e856/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/StaticRouteHandlerModel/EndpointParameter.cs#L595-L616)). The older `EndpointParameter.SignatureEquals` on `release/10.0` ([EndpointParameter.cs#L604-L611 at 55d77e1](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/55d77e1e0349aa2a079a516f6ecb7c79b56bf85c/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/StaticRouteHandlerModel/EndpointParameter.cs#L604-L611)) ignores it too. Yet the emitted code depends on it: the `Cast` delegate type is meant to capture default parameter values ([StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L19-L28](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/aaec58f9ccee7962c6071b36f5b17eb07af0e856/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/StaticRouteHandlerModel/StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L19-L28)), and the fallback carries the default value too.

Workaround: give the parameters different names. `[FromQuery(Name = "page")] int p = 2` keeps the query key unchanged and gives each handler its own interceptor.

### Expected Behavior

`GET /page-1` returns `page 1` and `GET /page-2` returns `page 2`, as with the generator off.

### Steps To Reproduce

Repro project: https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-rdg-default-value. `./repro.sh` builds and runs it with the generator off, then on; `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` does the same on .NET 11.

`Repro.csproj` (the repository's version takes the target framework from `REPRO_TFM`; `net10.0` is its default):

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <EnableRequestDelegateGenerator>true</EnableRequestDelegateGenerator>
    <EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>true</EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

`Program.cs`:

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateSlimBuilder(args);
builder.Logging.ClearProviders();
builder.WebHost.UseUrls("http://127.0.0.1:0");
var app = builder.Build();

app.MapGet("/page-1", (int page = 1) => $"page {page}");
app.MapGet("/page-2", (int page = 2) => $"page {page}");

await app.StartAsync();
using var client = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(app.Urls.First()) };
Console.WriteLine("GET /page-1 -> " + await client.GetStringAsync("/page-1"));
Console.WriteLine("GET /page-2 -> " + await client.GetStringAsync("/page-2"));
await app.StopAsync();
```

```
dotnet build -p:EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false && dotnet run --no-build   # page 1 / page 2
rm -rf bin obj && dotnet build && dotnet run --no-build                         # InvalidCastException
```

### Exceptions (if any)

```text
Unhandled exception. System.InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type '<>f__AnonymousDelegate1`2[System.Int32,System.String]' to type '<>f__AnonymousDelegate0`2[System.Int32,System.String]'.
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Generated.<GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensions_g>F705AFFC00BBE82D3AAC29F52EDC0EBE8384420EAFA5C35DC66A2FA28704C0DC3__GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensionsCore.Cast[T](Delegate d, T _) in <repro>\obj\Debug\net10.0\generated\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator.RequestDelegateGenerator\GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensions.g.cs:line 209
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Generated.<GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensions_g>F705AFFC00BBE82D3AAC29F52EDC0EBE8384420EAFA5C35DC66A2FA28704C0DC3__GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensionsCore.MapGet0(IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, String pattern, Delegate handler) in <repro>\obj\Debug\net10.0\generated\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator.RequestDelegateGenerator\GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensions.g.cs:line 182
   at Program.<Main>$(String[] args) in <repro>\Program.cs:line 7
   at Program.<Main>(String[] args)
```

The same exception on SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 with `net11.0`.

### .NET Version

10.0.401 (also 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128)

### Anything else?

- ASP.NET Core: 10.0.12 and 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 (the generator ships in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref`)
- No IDE (CLI); Windows 11 (10.0.26200) x64 and Ubuntu x64

Found while adding native AOT checks to [AdCodicem.ValueObjects](https://github.com/AdCodicem/AdCodicem.ValueObjects). Investigation and write-up assisted by Claude (Anthropic); the linked repro was run on Windows 11 and Ubuntu, and I reviewed this report.

Skip existing docs drafts by default; support verified no-op refreshes.

## Description

Adds a manual `existing_draft` choice with `skip` as the default and `refresh` as the explicit alternative. A read-only preparation job checks source eligibility and validates the existing automated draft's current identity before deciding whether to run the agent. Default reruns link the canonical draft in the job summary and skip inference, publication, and source/docs notifications. Source patches and version inputs are not fetched on this path. Both choices retain normal creation when no draft exists.

Explicit refresh keeps the existing push-plus-title contract for real updates, and adds a distinct `docs_pr_action: "unchanged"` outcome for sufficient existing documentation. That outcome requires exactly one no-op and one notification, a trusted selected draft, and post-agent evidence that working-tree content, staging, untracked files, and HEAD remain at the trusted original draft head. It also rechecks the live docs PR identity/head before attribution. A title-only `updated` outcome still fails rather than silently dropping edits. Sufficient refreshes report **already sufficient**, not **updated**, and retain the idempotent managed source-author body section without renaming the PR or replacing its generated/human-edited description. Matching non-draft or identity-mismatched automation PRs block replacement instead of authorizing duplicate creation.

Addresses the rerun failure reported in [run 37358446353](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/37358446353), where sufficient existing documentation led to a title-only update that violated the mandatory-push contract. The baseline validator independently reproduces that rejection. This preserves the manual-only merged-main gate, existing model/turn budget, token topology, command permissions, version resolution, context preparation, and author-attribution behavior. No gh-aw upgrade or unrelated workflow edits.

**Validation**

- `python -m unittest discover -s .github\workflows\pr-docs-check` — passed, 71 tests, no skips. Includes real temporary Git repositories executing the workflow's exact post-agent evidence script for clean, unstaged, staged, staged-but-restored, untracked, committed, and deleted-file cases; mocked API fixtures exercise the actual trusted preparation producer.
- `node --test .github\workflows\pr-docs-check\test_author_body.cjs` — passed, 9 tests, including execution of the actual attribution step for unchanged refreshes, repeat-write idempotence, preservation of human edits, and changed-identity rejection.
- `gh aw compile pr-docs-check --strict` — passed with repository-pinned gh-aw **v0.89.21**, no warnings; regenerated the lock file. Structured inspection also passed for dispatch defaults, agent dependencies/condition, skipped-agent publication conditions, and post-analysis evidence placement.
- `actionlint.exe -shellcheck= -pyflakes= -ignore 'unknown permission scope "copilot-requests"' -ignore 'property "safe-outputs-head-app-token" is not defined' -ignore 'unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section' -ignore 'property "aw" is not defined' .github\workflows\pr-docs-check.lock.yml` — passed with native actionlint v1.7.12. These exact four compiler/tooling diagnostics were also reproduced against the unchanged latest-main lock file; no new diagnostics. Optional ShellCheck and Pyflakes integrations were disabled.
- `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check` — passed.
- Local baseline fixture check loading `origin/main:.github/workflows/pr-docs-check/validate_outcome.py` — reproduced the required-push error for title-only `updated` and unsupported-action error for the sufficient `unchanged` fixture; the new sufficient-refresh contract passes.

**Boundary:** no production workflow was dispatched, no model inference was run, and [dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs#37773](https://github.com/dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs/pull/37773) was not modified. Live GitHub publication and model adherence to the revised prompt remain unexercised. No framework build was run because this change is confined to the documentation workflow and its helpers/tests.

Issues.Title: Default Blazor Web App emits SectionRenderModeMismatch warning for Counter PageTitle
Issues.Body:
## Describe the bug

An unmodified default Blazor Web App emits a `SectionRenderModeMismatch` warning when visiting the Counter page with the .NET 11 RC2 candidate build.

The application does not explicitly use `SectionOutlet` or `SectionContent`. The warning comes from the built-in `PageTitle`/`HeadOutlet` implementation and identifies the section only as `System.Object`, so it is not actionable to someone running the default template.

This appears to be a template/diagnostic-quality issue, not evidence of a new failure of the Counter page or its constant page title. The title displays correctly and the counter remains interactive.

## Steps to reproduce

With SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105` installed:

```powershell
dotnet new blazor -n BlazorApp
cd BlazorApp
dotnet run --launch-profile http
```

Visit `/counter`, either directly or through the navigation menu.

The generated `App.razor` contains:

```razor
<HeadOutlet />
...
<Routes />
```

The generated `Counter.razor` contains:

```razor
@page "/counter"
@rendermode InteractiveServer

<PageTitle>Counter</PageTitle>
```

## Actual behavior

```text
warn: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Sections.SectionRegistry[1]
      The section with ID 'System.Object' has its SectionOutlet in render mode 'static server-side rendering' and its SectionContent in render mode 'InteractiveServerRenderMode'. Sections cannot connect across render mode boundaries, so the outlet will not display this content once the components become interactive.
```

The title is still `Counter` after the page becomes interactive, and clicking the button increments the count. Navigating to Home and back to Counter also displays the expected titles. The warning occurs during server prerendering, before interactive startup.

Comparison runs:

| Configuration | Section mismatch warning |
| --- | --- |
| .NET 11 RC2 candidate, default per-page Server interactivity | Yes |
| .NET 11 RC2 candidate, `dotnet new blazor --all-interactive` | No |
| .NET 10 target, `dotnet new blazor -f net10.0`, running on `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.0.12` | No |

The .NET 10 control was generated using the installed SDK's `net10.0` template option, not a historical .NET 10 SDK.

## Expected behavior

The default template should not produce a warning about its own built-in page-title configuration during ordinary use. If this configuration warrants a warning, the diagnostic should identify `PageTitle`/`HeadOutlet` and explain the actual limitation and an appropriate remedy rather than exposing an opaque internal section ID.

Please reconcile the default per-page-interactivity template with the section diagnostic without suppressing useful warnings for unsupported user-defined sections.

## Investigation and related tracking

- The diagnostic was added as part of #66831 ("Add better warnings and errors for Sections"). Its implementation was intended to be observational rather than a change to section rendering.
- `HeadOutlet` creates a `SectionOutlet` using its internal `TitleSectionId` (`new object()`); `PageTitle` creates the corresponding `SectionContent`. In the default template the outlet is static and the Counter page content is Interactive Server, so `SectionRegistry.DetectRenderModeMismatch` logs the warning.

I searched open and closed issues before filing and did not find a report specifically tracking the default template emitting this new warning for its built-in, constant Counter page title. This report is scoped to that template/diagnostic interaction, not general cross-render-mode section support.

## Environment

- Windows x64
- .NET SDK: `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`
- `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App`: `11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105`
- Target framework: `net11.0`
- Default Blazor Web App: Server interactivity, per-page/component interactivity, no authentication

Add evidence-backed regression labeling to the issue-triage workflow.

## Description

Allow the issue-triage agent to apply `regression` when comparable before/after evidence identifies an earlier working and newer failing .NET / ASP.NET Core version, including servicing and successive preview builds. Require the same code or scenario, described expected and actual behavior, and comparable measurements for performance reports. Do not infer regressions from an upgrade or the word "regression" alone, unrelated application/environment changes, or documented intentional breaking changes.

Preserve existing issue types, area/sub-type labels, the three-label limit, and dry-run staging. Treat incomplete comparisons as reported but unconfirmed, request only missing evidence, and retain existing regression labels. Prevent the no-op path from suppressing a missing applicable regression label or new comparison information. Distinguish a reported failing version from the first affected version.

This is evidence-based triage, not automated cross-SDK reproduction. Attribute reporter-supplied results to the reporter. Do not follow issue links, download attachments, or execute issue/comment code, scripts, or commands.

Only `.github/workflows/issue-triage-agent.md` and its compiler-generated `.lock.yml` change. The source patch is preserved from the existing implementation commit. Regenerated the lock with the matching `gh-aw v0.89.21` compiler to resolve its metadata conflict with upstream, without compiler/reference churn. No public API changes.

Validation:
- `gh aw compile issue-triage-agent --strict --no-check-update` — passed with v0.89.21; recompiling produced no changes (`git diff --exit-code` passed).
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` — passed.
- PowerShell static parsed-JSON red/green checks against `HEAD^` — passed for both compiled safe-output configurations: the baseline excludes `regression`, the new configuration includes it, and every other setting is unchanged, including existing labels, `max: 3`, dry-run staging, and issue-type staging.

Summary of the changes (Less than 80 chars)

Fix incorrect object constraint for OpenAPI floating-point unions

## Description

Fixes #69604.

When `JsonNumberHandling.AllowNamedFloatingPointLiterals` is enabled, the
.NET 10 OpenAPI schema generation can produce an incorrect `object` type
constraint for a floating-point property using `anyOf`.

This makes the generated schema unsatisfiable because numeric values cannot
satisfy the outer `object` constraint.

reading `anyOf` and `oneOf` schemas.

A regression test has also been added to verify that named floating-point
literals generate the expected schema without the incorrect outer object
constraint.

behavior already corrected on main.

# Fix WebSocket accept context state leaking between connections

- [x] You've read the [[Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [[Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making.

Create a new `WebSocketAcceptContext` for each WebSocket acceptance.

## Description

`DefaultWebSocketManager.AcceptWebSocketAsync(string? subProtocol)` previously reused a static `WebSocketAcceptContext` when no subprotocol was specified.

Because `WebSocketAcceptContext` is mutable, components such as Interactive Server Components can modify properties such as `DangerousEnableCompression`. Reusing the same instance can cause those changes to persist and affect subsequent unrelated WebSocket connections.

This change removes the shared default context and creates a new `WebSocketAcceptContext` for each call to `AcceptWebSocketAsync`.

A regression test was also added to verify that enabling compression for one WebSocket connection does not leak into a subsequent connection using the default accept context.

The regression test was verified to:
- Fail against the existing implementation.
- Pass after applying this change.

Fixes #69652

> AI assistance was used to help prepare the pull request details.

Issues.Body:
This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

Issues.Title: Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?
Issues.Body:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)

Issues.Title: [Question] Passwords should not be of type String ?
Issues.Body:
My security team escalated to me that the `PasswordHasher` is vulnerable to heap inspection, as the password is of type `String`. 
It should be instead a byte array / span of bytes cleared at the end of the process, as it is done by any cryptographic operation in corefx. CC @bartonjs.
Same problem with any password related types (`IPasswordValidator`, and maybe also the `IUserPasswordStore`)

Issues.Title: Feedback: ensure that .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling only supported in VS 2017 and won't be supported in VS 2019
Issues.Body:
Apologize if my feedback may sound controversial or may spark a debate.

I need to be sure that the problem mentioned on this [page](https://github.com/aspnet/Tooling/blob/master/known-issues-vs2017.md#to-create-aspnet-core-10--11-projects-install-visual-studios-net-core-10---11-developer-tools-for-web-component) about .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling is installed when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project should not happen or should not be supported in VS 2019.

These are my main concerns:

1. VS 2019 is about to be released in around early 2019
2. ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 is not going to be supported anymore, based on [this page](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/master/microsoft-support.md).
3. Creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 will always install the .NET Core 1.0/1.1 web tooling, and this is not necessary when previous reason has reached the unsupported period and it's quite near or might be the same time of VS 2019 release.
4. Based on the problem mentioned above, VS 2017 has no "built in" tooling when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project, but the external tooling may help. Therefore for those that still need to maintain ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 projects, we could use VS 2017 as long as the VS 2017 is still in support lifecycle or in mainstream support lifecycle.

I welcome feedback 🙂
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Feedback: ensure that .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling only supported in VS 2017 and won't be supported in VS 2019" (#1078)

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the OpenID Connect handler validates the signed ID token `auth_time` claim whenever `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge` causes an effective `max_age` value to be sent.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69321 and addresses https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67462.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

The handler sent `max_age` on the authorization request but did not validate the returned ID token's `auth_time`. Applications relied entirely on the identity provider to honor the request. A missing, malformed, stale, or excessively future `auth_time` did not cause authentication to fail.

### New behavior

When an effective `max_age` is sent, the handler correlates the exact value through protected authorization-transaction state and validates every ID token used by the supported authorization flow after normal token and OpenID Connect protocol validation.

The `auth_time` claim must be an integral, nonnegative OpenID Connect NumericDate. Authentication fails when the claim is missing, malformed, fractional, negative, overflowed, later than the current time plus `OpenIdConnectOptions.TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew`, or older than `max_age` plus that clock skew. Exact boundaries and values within skew are accepted.

The validation covers authorization-code, implicit, and hybrid flows, including both relevant ID tokens in hybrid flows, and both the default `TokenHandler` path and legacy `SecurityTokenValidator` path. No validation occurs when no `max_age` is configured. In addition to the `MaxAge` properties, applications can configure the parameter through `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` or `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

OpenID Connect Core requires the authorization server to include `auth_time` when `max_age` is requested and recommends that the relying party validate it. Correlating and checking the signed assertion prevents a missing or nonconforming assertion from silently satisfying an application's configured maximum authentication age.

The guarantee remains limited to the trusted identity provider's signed assertion. ASP.NET Core cannot prove that a particular physical authentication ceremony occurred and cannot protect against a compromised identity provider that signs false data. This change does not revalidate UserInfo, refresh-token redemption, local cookie lifetime, or physical user interaction.

### Recommended action

Ensure that identity providers emit a valid signed `auth_time` and honor the requested `max_age` whenever the application configures that parameter, most commonly through `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`.

For a temporarily incompatible provider, restore the previous request-only behavior by setting the process-wide compatibility switch before authentication starts:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation",
    true);
```

The equivalent runtime configuration is:

```json
{
  "runtimeOptions": {
    "configProperties": {
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation": true
    }
  }
}
```

The switch defaults to `false` and is intended only as a temporary provider-compatibility escape hatch.

When pushed authorization is used, set or modify `max_age` in `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`. Changing it later in `OnPushAuthorization` is rejected while validation is active unless pushing is skipped, because the handler has already correlated the value with the authorization response.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. The behavioral change affects applications that set:

- `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectOptions.AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` when it includes `max_age`
- `OpenIdConnectEvents.OnRedirectToIdentityProvider` when it sets `max_age`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time" (#537)

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Identity external login keys use ordinal equality
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the built-in Entity Framework Core Identity stores verify external-login `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values using managed ordinal equality after the indexed database lookup returns a candidate.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69277.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

`UserStore` and `UserOnlyStore` filtered external logins with a database-translated equality predicate. The database collation therefore determined whether the stored `(LoginProvider, ProviderKey)` tuple matched the supplied values.

On a case-insensitive collation, `FindByLoginAsync` could resolve a login whose provider name or provider key differed only by case. On databases where equality ignores trailing spaces, it could also resolve a key that differed by trailing spaces. `RemoveLoginAsync` used the same collation-dependent lookup and could remove such a login.

### New behavior

The database equality remains the indexed candidate lookup. The built-in EF Identity stores then require the returned `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` to match the requested values using `StringComparison.Ordinal`.

A collation-only match now causes `FindByLoginAsync` to return no user and `RemoveLoginAsync` to perform no removal. Exact ordinal matches continue to work.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

External provider keys are opaque identifiers whose equality must not vary with the configured database provider or collation. Managed ordinal verification makes the built-in EF stores consistent with the in-memory reference store while preserving the existing indexed database lookup.

### Recommended action

Ensure that applications persist and later supply the exact `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values issued for an external login. Do not normalize, case-fold, trim, or otherwise alter provider keys.

Third-party `IUserLoginStore<TUser>` implementations own their equality semantics. Implementations that query a collation-aware database should preserve an indexed candidate lookup and verify the materialized provider name and key with ordinal equality before resolving or removing a login.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. This behavioral change affects the built-in Entity Framework Core implementations of:

- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.FindByLoginAsync`
- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.RemoveLoginAsync`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Blazor server-side rendering defers antiforgery validation to middleware
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, Blazor static server-side rendering (SSR) endpoints no longer validate antiforgery tokens themselves. They rely on the antiforgery verdict recorded by upstream middleware and generate antiforgery tokens only when token-based antiforgery middleware is present.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67082.

### Version

.NET 11 Preview 6

### Previous behavior

When a Blazor SSR endpoint handled a form `POST`, the endpoint validated the request itself if antiforgery middleware hadn't already recorded a result.

The endpoint also generated and stored antiforgery tokens for rendered forms even when `app.UseAntiforgery()` wasn't present in the pipeline.

Consequently, apps that didn't call `app.UseAntiforgery()` still emitted and validated antiforgery tokens.

### New behavior

Blazor SSR endpoints now trust the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` verdict recorded by upstream middleware. A form `POST` is rejected with `400 Bad Request` when the recorded verdict is invalid.

The verdict can be recorded by:

- Token-based antiforgery middleware added by `app.UseAntiforgery()` (explicit usage).
- Automatic cross-origin CSRF protection middleware added by default to apps built with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`.

Blazor SSR endpoints no longer call `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync` directly. Antiforgery tokens are generated only when token-based antiforgery middleware ran for the request.

Apps using `app.UseAntiforgery()` retain token-based validation. Apps without it rely on automatic cross-origin CSRF protection and no longer emit antiforgery tokens for their forms.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Token-based antiforgery and automatic cross-origin CSRF protection now record a shared verdict through `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature`.

Validating again inside the Blazor SSR endpoint duplicated work and could produce a result different from the middleware verdict. Generating tokens without token-based antiforgery middleware also produced tokens that nothing validated.

### Recommended action

If your Blazor SSR app relies on antiforgery tokens for form validation or rendering, ensure that it calls `app.UseAntiforgery()`:
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseAntiforgery();
```

If you were not calling `app.UseAntiforgery()` before you will start using CSRF protection as the defense mechanism from now on.

### Affected APIs

None. This is a behavioral change affecting Blazor SSR form processing and antiforgery-token generation.

# ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 13, 2027

> Update: The ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support date was updated from April 7, 2027 to April 13, 2027 to align with the Microsoft servicing release cycles.

Today we are announcing that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach **end of support on April 13, 2027**. After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide security patches, bug fixes, or technical support for ASP.NET Core 2.3.

This announcement provides the required 12 months of advance notice, as defined by the [Microsoft Support Lifecycle Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/faq/general-lifecycle#what-is-the-lifecycle-policy-for-tools-) for products classified as "Tools."

## Current support policy

ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages (latest patched version only) are currently [supported](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/aspnet#dotnet-core) on .NET Framework, following the support cycle for those .NET Framework versions. After April 13, 2027, this support will end regardless of the .NET Framework version in use.

Note that the [ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/aspnet/2.3-packages) include the Entity Framework 2.3 packages, which will end support on the same date.

## Impact of end of support

After ASP.NET Core 2.3 reaches end of support:

- No new security updates will be issued for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- Continuing to use an unsupported version may expose your applications to security vulnerabilities.
- Technical support will no longer be available for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- The ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages will be deprecated.

## Upgrade recommendation

We recommend upgrading to a [currently supported version of .NET](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet), such as .NET 10 (LTS).

To help with the upgrade process, we recommend using [GitHub Copilot modernization](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/porting/github-copilot-app-modernization/overview), which provides AI-powered assistance to help you analyze, plan, and execute your migration to a modern .NET version.

Issues.Title: Add automation to create docs tracking issues for breaking changes
Issues.Body:
Automates creation of documentation tracking issues in `dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs` when breaking change issues are opened or labeled in this repository.

## Implementation

**New workflow:** `.github/workflows/create-docs-issue.yaml`

- Triggers on `issues.opened` and `issues.labeled` events with "Breaking change" label
- Creates issue in docs repo with:
  - Title: `[Breaking Change] <original title>`
  - Body: Link to source issue, full context
  - Labels: `breaking-change`, `aspnet/Announcements`
- Posts comment on source issue with link to docs issue

## Duplicate Prevention

Multi-layer detection to handle race conditions and partial failures:
- Checks for existing bot comments in source issue
- Searches docs repo by title before creating
- Concurrency control keyed on issue number

## Error Handling

Separate try-catch blocks for each operation:
- Comment listing failures → proceed with search
- Search failures → proceed with creation (fail open to avoid missing docs)
- Comment posting failures → don't fail workflow (docs issue already created)
- Permission errors → explicit message about `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` requirement

## Setup Required

Configure `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` repository secret with `repo` scope for cross-repository issue creation. Falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` but will fail with clear error message.

Explicit minimal permissions: `issues: write`, `contents: read`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Deprecating WebHostBuilder,  IWebHost, and WebHost
Issues.Body:
### Description

`WebHostBuilder` was replaced by `HostBuilder` ([generic host](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder)) in 3.0 and we also added [`WebApplicationBuilder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) in 6.0.

We are now marking `WebHostBuilder` as obsolete to encourage users to move on to the alternatives which is where future investments will occur, and we're also marking `IWebHost` and `WebHost` as deprecated to clean up other parts of the now obsolete web host story.

### Version

.NET 10 RC 1

### Previous behavior

```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

### New behavior

Using `WebHostBuilder` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR004**:
> warning ASPDEPR004: WebHostBuilder is deprecated in favor of HostBuilder and WebApplicationBuilder. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/004.

Using `IWebHost` or `WebHost` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR008**:
> warning ASPDEPR008: WebHost is obsolete. Use HostBuilder or WebApplicationBuilder instead. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/008.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [x] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

We recommend the use of `HostBuilder` and `WebApplication` going forward over `WebHostBuilder` because they have all the features of `WebHostBuilder` and will be the focus of future investment.

### Recommended action

See https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/host/generic-host or https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/minimal-apis/webapplication for more details on the different hosting models. As well as [HostBuilder replaces WebHostBuilder](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder) and [Introducing WebApplication](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) for migration guides.

Below is an example of converting `WebHostBuilder` to `HostBuilder`:

**Before**
```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

**After**
```csharp
using var host = new HostBuilder()
    .ConfigureWebHost(webHostBuilder =>
    {
        webHostBuilder
            .UseTestServer() // If using TestServer
            .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
            .UseStartup()
            .UseKestrel();
    })
    .Build();
await host.StartAsync();

var testServer = host.GetTestServer();
```

Both Copilot and ChatGpt have given good results so far when asked to convert a WebHostBuilder example to use HostBuilder. Below is an example prompt:
<details>
<summary>Example AI Prompt</summary>

> Can you convert
>
> var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
>     .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
>     .UseStartup()
>     .UseKestrel();
> // Test code might use TestServer:
> var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
>
> to use HostBuilder.

</details>

### Affected APIs

`public class Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.WebHostBuilder`
`public interface Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.IWebHost`
`public static class Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebHost`

### Discussion

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/63480

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Exception diagnostics are suppressed when `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true
Issues.Body:
### Description

The [ASP.NET Core exception handler middleware](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#exception-handler-page), `UseExceptionHandler()`, is responsible for catching and processing unhandled exceptions from ASP.NET Core requests.

In .NET 8, we introduced [`IExceptionHandler`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#iexceptionhandler). Implementations of `IExceptionHandler` are registered with dependency injection and invoked by the middleware. An implementation can return `true` from `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` to indicate that the exception has been handled. The middleware stops processing the exception once it has been handled.

In .NET 10, we're changing the default behavior so that the middleware no longer records diagnostics for exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

### Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

### Previous behavior

The exception handler middleware recorded diagnostics about exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

The exception diagnostics are:

- Logging `UnhandledException` to `ILogger`.
- Writing the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HandledException` event to `EventSource`.
- Adding the `error.type` tag to the `http.server.request.duration` metric.

### New behavior

If `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns `true`, then exception diagnostics are no longer recorded by default.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

ASP.NET Core users have given feedback that the previous behavior was undesirable. Their `IExceptionHandler` implementation reported that the exception was handled, but the error handling middleware still recorded the error in the app's telemetry.

We are changing ASP.NET Core to follow the behavior expected by users by suppressing diagnostics when `IExceptionHandler` handles the exception. We're also adding configuration options to customize exception diagnostics behavior if needed.

### Recommended action

If you want handled exceptions to continue recording telemetry, you can use the new `ExceptionHandlerOptions.SuppressDiagnosticsCallback` option:

```cs
app.UseExceptionHandler(new ExceptionHandlerOptions
{
    SuppressDiagnosticsCallback = context => false;
});
```

The context passed to the callback includes information about the exception, the request, and whether the exception was handled. Returning `false` from the callback indicates that diagnostics shouldn't be suppressed. This restores the previous behavior.

### References

- Issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54554
- PR: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/59074

### Affected APIs

- `UseExceptionHandler()`
- `IExceptionHandler`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and MVC API analyzers are deprecated
Issues.Body:
## Description

The `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` MSBuild property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. When `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will now emit warning `ASPDEPR007`.

## Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

## Previous behavior

Previously, developers could set `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` in their Web SDK projects to enable MVC API analyzers without any warnings or deprecation notices.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework>
    <IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

The project would build successfully without any deprecation warnings.

## New behavior

Starting in .NET 10 Preview 7, when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will emit warning `ASPDEPR007`:

```
warning ASPDEPR007: The IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
```

The analyzers will continue to function, but developers will receive this deprecation warning during compilation.

## Type of breaking change

- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

## Reason for change

## Reason for change

The MVC API analyzers were originally introduced to help keep return types and attributes in sync for API controllers, ensuring consistency between method signatures and their corresponding OpenAPI documentation. These analyzers provided compile-time validation to catch mismatches between declared return types and the actual types returned by controller actions.

However, with the introduction of Minimal APIs and the `TypedResults` pattern, the .NET ecosystem has evolved toward a more type-safe approach for API development. `TypedResults` provides compile-time guarantees about response types without requiring additional analyzers, making the MVC API analyzers redundant for modern .NET applications. In .NET 10, `TypedResults` are supported in controller-based APIs.

**Previous approach with MVC API analyzers:**
```csharp
[HttpGet]
[ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)]
[ProducesResponseType(404)]
public async Task<ActionResult> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    if (product == null)
        return NotFound(); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType(404)
    
    return Ok(product); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)
}
```

**Or with controller actions using TypedResults:**
```csharp
[HttpGet("{id}")]
public async Task<Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    return product == null 
        ? TypedResults.NotFound() 
        : TypedResults.Ok(product);
}
```

The `TypedResults` pattern eliminates the need for separate analyzers because the return type itself (`Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>`) explicitly declares all possible response types at compile time. This approach is more maintainable, provides better IntelliSense support, and automatically generates accurate OpenAPI documentation without additional tooling.

As the .NET ecosystem continues to embrace `TypedResults` as the recommended pattern for API development, the MVC API analyzers have become obsolete and are being deprecated to streamline the development experience.

## Recommended action

Developers should:

1. **Remove the deprecated property**: Remove `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` from your project files to eliminate the warning.

2. **Suppress the warning temporarily**: If you need to continue using the deprecated analyzers temporarily, you can suppress the warning:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);ASPDEPR007</NoWarn>
</PropertyGroup>
```

3. **Migrate to TypedResults**: Migrate to the `TypedResults` pattern documented above to ensure better consistency between application behavior and OpenAPI documentation.

## Affected APIs

- MSBuild property: `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers`
- Associated MVC API analyzers included when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is `true`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Forwarded Headers Middleware Now Ignores X-Forwarded-* Headers from Unknown Proxies
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 8.0.17 and 9.0.6, the Forwarded Headers Middleware will ignore all `X-Forwarded-*` headers from proxies that are not explicitly configured as trusted.

### Version

.NET 8

### Previous behavior

Previously, the middleware, when not configured to use `X-Forwarded-For`, would process `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and `X-Forwarded-Host` headers from any source, potentially allowing malicious or misconfigured proxies/clients to spoof these headers and affect your application's understanding of client information.

### New behavior

With this change, only headers sent by known, trusted proxies (as configured via `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownProxies` and `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownNetworks`) will be processed. Headers from unknown sources will be ignored.

**This is a breaking change**: If your deployment relied on forwarded headers from proxies not configured in your application's trusted proxy list, those headers will no longer be honored.

This can cause behavior like infinite redirects if you're using the Https redirection middleware and using TLS termination in your proxy. Or authentication to fail if using TLS termination and expecting an https request.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The change was made for security hardening, as the proxy and IP lists weren't being applied in all cases.

### Recommended action

- **Review your deployment topology:**  
  Ensure that all legitimate proxy servers in front of your app are properly added to `KnownProxies` or `KnownNetworks` in your `ForwardedHeadersOptions` configuration.
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownProxies = { IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_PROXY_IP") }
  });
  ```
  Or, for a network:
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownNetworks = { new IPNetwork(IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_NETWORK_IP"), PREFIX_LENGTH) }
  });
  ```

- **If you wish to enable previous behavior:**  
  You may need to relax your configuration, but this is **not recommended** due to security risks. You can do this by clearing the `KnownNetworks` and `KnownProxies` lists in `ForwardedHeadersOptions` to allow any proxy or network to forward these headers.

You can also set the `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` environment variable to true, which clears the lists and enables `ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto`.

For applications targeting .NET 9.0 or less, you can set the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides.IgnoreUnknownProxiesWithoutFor` [AppContext](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/runtime-libraries/system-appcontext) switch to `"true"` or `1` to get back to the previous behavior. Alternatively, set the `MICROSOFT_ASPNETCORE_HTTPOVERRIDES_IGNORE_UNKNOWN_PROXIES_WITHOUT_FOR` environment variable.

> [!Note]
> In cloud environments, the proxy IP(s) can change over the lifetime of the app and `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` is sometimes used to make forwarded headers work.

### References

- [Forwarded Headers Middleware documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/proxy-load-balancer)

### Affected APIs

`UseForwardedHeaders();`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Legacy Mono and Emscripten JavaScript APIs are not exported to global namespace in Blazor WebAssembly applications
Issues.Body:
### Description

In previous versions of Blazor WebAssembly, legacy Mono and Emscripten APIs were exported to global namespace. 
From 9.0 those APIs are accessible throught Blazor.runtime object.

### Version

.NET 9 GA

### Previous behavior

Legacy Mono (MONO, BINDING) and Emscripten Module object was exported to global window object.
For example `window.Module.FS` returned emscripten virtual filesystem.

### New behavior

Emscripten Module object is now exported to `Blazor.runtime` object.
For example `Blazor.runtime.Module.FS` returns emscripten virtual filesystem.
Legacy Mono API for interop was removed completely (MONO and BINDING) and replaced with JSImport/JSExport.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The general goal is not to polute global namespace and keep all the APIs accessible from single Blazor object.

### Recommended action

Replace accessing Emscripten APIs from window object to Blazor.runtime object.

### Affected APIs

window.MONO.*
window.BINDING.*
window.Module.*

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: dev cert export no longer creates folder
Issues.Body:
### Description

When you export the ASP.NET Core development certificate (used to enable https in local development), it will no longer create the directory into which the certificate is being exported, if that directory doesn’t already exist.

This change first appears in 8.0.10 and 9.0 RC1.

### Version

.NET 8 GA

### Previous behavior

```
dotnet dev-certs https -ep C:\NonExistent\cert.pfx
```

If `C:\NonExistent\` did not exist when the command was run, it would be created (with permissions inherited from the containing directory).

### New behavior

The target directory must exist or the export will fail with a message like `There was an error exporting the HTTPS developer certificate to a file.`

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [X] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The development certificate is exported with its private key, so unauthorized access can be very problematic.  It may, nevertheless, be necessary to make it readable to multiple accounts - e.g. if the consuming process will not be run as the current user.  Rather than attempting to determine (and securely establish) permissions for the target directory, `dotnet dev-certs` require that it already exist.

### Recommended action

Create the target directory (with appropriate permissions) before invoking `dotnet dev-certs`.

### Affected APIs

This functionality is not presently exposed via an API - it is invoked from the command line.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Handling of middleware types with multiple constructors
Issues.Body:
### Description

Formerly, when a middleware type with multiple satisfiable constructors was instantiated from the dependency injection container, the one with the most parameters would be used.  Now that only happens if the dependency injection container implements [`IServiceProviderIsService`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/microsoft.extensions.dependencyinjection.iserviceproviderisservice).

### Version

.NET 9 RC 1

### Previous behavior

Formerly, the first constructor was preferred (when both were satisfied) because it has more parameters.

```csharp
public class CookiePolicyMiddleware
{
    public CookiePolicyMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, IOptions<CookiePolicyOptions> options, ILoggerFactory factory)
    {
        // Omitted for brevity
    }

    public CookiePolicyMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, IOptions<CookiePolicyOptions> options)
    {
        // Omitted for brevity
    }
}
```

### New behavior

Now, neither constructor is preferred and construction fails with an error like 
```
System.InvalidOperationException: 'Multiple constructors accepting all given argument types have been found in type 'Microsoft.AspNetCore.CookiePolicy.CookiePolicyMiddleware'. There should only be one applicable constructor.'
```

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [X] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The activation mechanism was [changed](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/55722) to help support keyed dependency injection.

### Recommended action

If this happens and you can't upgrade to a dependency injection container that implements `IServiceProviderIsService`, you can add `ActivatorUtilitiesConstructorAttribute` to the preferred constructor of the affected middleware type.

### Affected APIs

This is [known](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/57231) to cause errors when instantiating `Microsoft.AspNetCore.CookiePolicy.CookiePolicyMiddleware` with [Autofac.Extensions.DependencyInjection](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Autofac.Extensions.DependencyInjection) 7.x.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: DefaultKeyResolution.ShouldGenerateNewKey has a slightly altered meaning
Issues.Body:
### Description

`DefaultKeyResolution.ShouldGenerateNewKey` no longer reflects whether the default key is close to its expiration time.

### Version

.NET 9 Preview 3

### Previous behavior

It was an undocumented, but consistent, feature of the API that `ShouldGenerateNewKey` would be true if the default key was within two days (an over-simplification) of its expiration time.  The amount of lead time was based on the polling interval of `ICacheableKeyRingProvider`, which was not something `IDefaultKeyResolver.ResolveDefaultKeyPolicy` should have depended upon (since, for example, alternative implementations would probably not be aware of these details).

### New behavior

If `ShouldGenerateNewKey` is true, it now indicates that either there is no default key or that for some other policy reason (i.e. in a specialized implementation of `IDefaultKeyResolver`, a new key should be generated.  The `ICacheableKeyRingProvider` will make its own decision about whether the expiration time is close enough to warrant generating a new key.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [X] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

First, we wanted to change the logic around key generation near expiration time and, second, this makes it more straightforward to implement a custom `IDefaultKeyResolver`.

Note that the documentation for this type already states that "This API supports infrastructure and is not intended to be used directly from your code. This API may change or be removed in future releases."

### Recommended action

If you have an `IDefaultKeyResolver` implementation that tries to replicate the expiry logic, that logic can be removed (however, leaving it is fine as well).

If you were consuming `IDefaultKeyResolver` directly, for the express purpose of determining whether expiration was pending and that continues to be important, you can the default key's `ExpirationDate` property directly.

### Affected APIs

Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection.KeyManagement.Internal.DefaultKeyResolution.ShouldGenerateNewKey

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Minimal APIs consuming IFormFile or IFormFileCollection parameters require anti-forgery checks
Issues.Body:
### Description

Minimal API endpoints that consume an `IFormFile` or `IFormFileCollection` will now be opted-in to requiring anti-forgery token validation using the new anti-forgery middleware.

### Version

.NET 8 RC 1

### Previous behavior

Minimal API endpoints that bound a parameter from the form via `IFormFile` or `IFormFileCollection` did not require anti-forgery validation.

### New behavior

Minimal API endpoints that bound a parameter from the form via `IFormFile` or `IFormFileCollection` did require anti-forgery validation. An exception will be thrown if the anti-forgery middleware is not registered for an API that defines these input types.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [X] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Anti-forgery token validation is a recommended security precaution for APIs that consume data from a form.

### Recommended action

Users can opt out of anti-forgery validation for specific endpoints by using the `DisableAntiforgery` method like so:

```csharp
var app = WebApplication.Create();

app.MapPost("/", (IFormFile formFile) => ...)
  .DisableAntiforgery();

app.Run();
```

### Affected APIs

None.
